page.title: Webinar Production Cost Breakdown and Planning
page.description: Learn what drives webinar production costs, typical price ranges, staffing needs, and how to plan your budget and timeline for your next virtual event.
page.definition: Webinar production cost is the total spend for crew, platform, rehearsal, backup stream, and edited deliverables, separate from platform licence fees, and varies by format complexity and staffing level. It covers producer, speaker management, branded assets, live moderation, recording, and clips.
page.quick_answer: Budget $2,500 to $7,500 for a moderated webinar and plan three to four weeks from brief to live; lock platform and run of show early.

sections.h2: What are the main cost models for webinar platforms?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate: per-host licences sized by attendee capacity, self-serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales.

ul: Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars)
Annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)

sections.h2: What does a produced webinar include and what does it cost?

blocks.p: A produced webinar delivers run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips, with moderated webinars ranging from $2,500 to $7,500 per production.

sections.h2: How long does production take and what are the key milestones?

blocks.p: Allow two to three weeks from brief to live for a webinar, with a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before and a technical check 60 minutes before going live.

ol: Production planning and run of show
Edited recording and clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: What staffing do you need for a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: One producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

ul: Webinar: single producer handles run of show, speaker cues, Q&A, backup stream
Summit: show caller owns timing, speaker manager preps presenters, moderator runs chat and Q&A, platform operator manages streaming and recording

sections.h2: How do you avoid scope creep and hidden fees?

blocks.p: Lock the platform and run of show before finalising the agenda, define deliverables up front, and assign one owner per workstream.

ul: Agree on run of show and rehearsal schedule early
Confirm backup stream and recording requirements
Set approval gates for each production stage
Use a shared plan in Asana, Monday.com or Airtable to track owners and outputs

faq.q: Can I use my existing platform for a produced webinar?
faq.a: Yes, production works on the platform you already use such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard; the crew joins your instance and runs the show without requiring a new licence.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform cost and production cost?
faq.a: Platform cost is the software licence for streaming; production cost covers the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show, rehearsal, backup stream and edited deliverables. They are two separate purchases.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book production for a summit?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. A summit needs six to eight weeks of management.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions sell event software?
faq.a: West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.

faq.q: What is the typical turnaround for the replay?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event; the edited recording and clips are part of the standard deliverables.
